paragraphs.text: MCP bridge for driving DeepSeek Harness sessions from Claude Code and other MCP clients
# ♡ dsh-session-bridge ♡
**Let your MCP client talk to DeepSeek Harness sessions~**
English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文
`@stellarie/dsh-session-bridge` (≧∀≦)
> Unofficial. This project has no tie to DeepSeek. It targets DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.3`. It also
runs on `0.2.1-rc.2`.
## What is this?
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is a desktop agent app. This package lets another agent drive it.
You get two small parts:

- **A host plugin.** It runs inside the DSH app. It serves a token-guarded loopback HTTP bridge.
- *
*A stdio MCP server.** Your MCP client (Claude Code, for example) starts it. It talks to the bridge.

Your client opens a normal DSH session, sends it messages, waits for the reply, and reads it.
The se
ssion shows in the app like any other session. You can watch it, or take it over, any time ♡
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.3` or `0.2.1-rc.2`, with a profile you can edit.
- Node.js `^22.19.0` o

r `>=24.0.0`.
- An MCP client that speaks stdio.

Any other MCP client works too. The command is `dsh-session-bridge-mcp`. The transport is stdio.
The MCP server reads the endpoint file on every call. An app restart needs no MCP restart.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `dsh_list_sessions` | List sessions: id, title, preset, working directory, running or idle. |
| `d
sh_open_session` | Open a session in the Workspace of `cwd`. The app creates the Workspace when none
exists. Reuses the newest idle session with the same `preset` and `cwd`. Pass `reuse: false` for a

new one. A new session starts at `effort` (default `high`). |
| `dsh_send` | Send a message. Mode `q

ueue` runs after the current turn. Mode `steer` joins the running turn. Returns `afterSeq`. |
| `dsh

_wait` | Wait until the session ends a turn after `afterSeq`. Default 600 s, maximum 600 s. |
| `dsh
_read` | Read your prompts and the assistant text after `afterSeq`. Tool calls and thinking are left

out. |
| `dsh_cancel` | Interrupt the running turn. Queued messages stay queued. |

## How the bridge stays safe (｀ω´)ゞ
The bridge gives full owner control of your sessions. Read this part, please.
Every request must pass these checks, in this order:

1. No `Origin` header. Browser pages always send one, so they are refused.
2. A loopback `Host` (`12

7.0.0.1`, `localhost`, or `[::1]`) with the server port.
3. A bearer token, compared in constant tim

e.
4. `POST` only, with a JSON body of at most 1 MiB.
5. A method on the allowlist. Session methods:
`create`, `prompt`, `page`, `projections`, `list`, `cancel`, `selectModel`, `modelCatalog`. Workspa
ce method: `create`.

The token is 32 random bytes. The plugin mints a new one at each start.
It writes `endpoint.json` (`
url`, `token`, `pid`, `startedAt`) with mode `0600` (POSIX) and deletes it on shutdown.

- **Treat the endpoint file as a secret.** Anyone who reads it can prompt your agents.
- The bridge

listens only where the DSH web server listens. It adds no port of its own.
- The bridge speaks as th

e app owner. A prompt you send acts like a prompt you type in the app.
- `dsh_open_session` creates
a Workspace for `cwd` when none exists, and it saves the new session's effort as the app default.
## Configuration
| Setting | Where | Default |
| `endpointPath` | plugin config in `cordis.patch.yml` | `$DSH_HOME/session-bridge/endpoint.json` |

| `DSH_SESSION_BRIDGE_ENDPOINT` | environment of the MCP server | unset |
| `DSH_HOME` | environment

N_BRIDGE_ENDPOINT` | environment of the MCP server | unset |
| `DSH_HOME` | environment | `~/.dsh` |
Set the same path on both sides when you move the file.
